column2: 108 hitters: nine per team by sportsbook book-market observation count. Expected lineup breaks ties and supplements a team with fewer than nine posted hitters.
12 starters: one per team. Projection = 2×K + 0.75×outs − 0.6×hits allowed − 0.6×walks − 2×earned runs.

Live no-vig multi-book hits, walks, and earned-run markets are used where posted. Missing hits/walks use expected innings × season WHIP; missing earned runs use expected innings × season ERA/9. The 75/25 hits/walks display split does not change their combined DK deduction.
Two-sided over/under prices are converted to implied probabilities and normalized to sum to 100%. Book-level estimates are aggregated by the median.
Hit, total-base, run, homer, and stolen-base ladders estimate expected counts using tail-sum probabilities. One-sided ladder prices are calibrated to overlapping no-vig two-sided markets.
Expected hits and total bases set the total volume. Singles, doubles, triples, and home-run markets allocate the hit mix while preserving both totals.
Daily books did not consistently offer batter BB/HBP markets. This small component uses the player's current-season BB+HBP-to-hit rate when available.
Rows with fewer than 35 book-market observations are blended toward a robust role-based prior. The prior is 75% same-lineup-slot/team market median and 25% winsorized DK AvgPointsPerGame.
High: 45+ observations; Medium: 20–44; Low: 8–19; Very low: fewer than 8.
The source showed expected rather than confirmed lineups at collection time. Market-frequency selection intentionally leaves some non-expected hitters in the 108-player test set.
